proposals.before: Yet in the age of Tang and Yu, when it was said that "the black-haired people were obstructed by famine," Yi Ji had to be appointed; when "the common people were not affectionate and the five relations were not in order," Qi had to be appointed — from this one knows that harmonious success cannot be assured, just as filial piety and friendship are not easily obtained.
proposals.after: Yet in the age of Tang and Yu, when it was said that "the black-haired people were obstructed by famine," Ji had to be appointed; when "the common people were not affectionate and the five relations were not in order," Qi had to be appointed — from this one knows that harmonious success cannot be assured, just as filial piety and friendship are not easily obtained.
proposals.reason: The literal adds an erroneous "Yi" before Ji; the Chinese has only 稷 (Ji).

proposals.before: Zhao Zhi, styled Jingdao, was a descendant of Sixianwen of the Liao.
proposals.after: Zhao Zhi, styled Jingdao, was a descendant of Siwen, a chancellor of the Liao.
proposals.reason: Chinese 遼相思溫 means Liao chancellor Siwen; "Sixianwen" wrongly fuses 相 with 思溫.

decisions.reason: s0009 has 不免以命稷, naming only 稷 (Ji); the literal's "Yi Ji" invents a syllable absent from the Chinese.
遼相思溫 is Liao chancellor Siwen (相 = office; 思溫 = name); "Sixianwen" wrongly fuses the title into the personal name.
The same 遼相思溫 parsing applies to the literal: 相 is chancellor and 思溫 is Siwen, so "Sixianwen" must be split.

This unit's Chinese is 薛繼元, so Xue Jiyuan is the accurate rendering; Wikisource preserves the section heading 薛繼元 while the biography opens 薛繼先, a transmitted heading/body discrepancy, not a translation error to silently emend.
